svg.text: Vaginal bleeding in pregnancy: reading it by gestation and by pain
First ask: before 24 weeks, or after? Then ask: is there pain, and is the uterus hard or soft?
EARLY — before 24 weeks
Miscarriage: cramping central pain, bleeding,
cervical os open or closed depending on type
Ectopic: amenorrhoea, unilateral pain, shock
out of proportion, shoulder tip pain
Molar: excessive vomiting, uterus large for
dates, grape-like tissue passed
Always do a pregnancy test. Always.
LATE — after 24 weeks
PRAEVIA: painless, bright red, SOFT uterus,
high presenting part, often recurrent
ABRUPTION: constant pain, dark blood,
HARD tender uterus, shock out of proportion
RUPTURE: contractions stop, constant pain,
foetal parts easily felt, collapse
NO digital vaginal examination until scanned.
The one distinction to hold on to
SOFT uterus, PAINLESS bleeding → think PRAEVIA
HARD uterus, PAINFUL bleeding → think ABRUPTION
And in abruption the visible loss lies to you, because most of the blood is trapped behind the placenta.
While you wait for the doctor, in any of them
Two large cannulae · Blood for grouping and cross-match · Fluids running · Observations every 15 minutes
Nil by mouth · Foetal heart · Catheter and fluid balance · Consent and theatre alerted · Call the blood bank early
Resuscitate against her pulse and blood pressure, never against the size of the stain.
